etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Medieval Latin populātus, past participle of populor (“populate”), from Latin populus (“people”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To supply with inhabitants; to people.
(intransitive) To increase in number; to breed.
(computing, transitive, intransitive) To fill initially empty items in a collection.
(electronics) To fill initially empty slots or sockets on a circuit board or similar.

quote.citation: a. 1626, Francis Bacon, Bacon Verulam, Viscount St. Albans, “Notes of a Speech, concerning a War with Spaine”, in Letters, Memoirs, Parliamentary Affairs, State Papers, &c., London: Robert Stephens, published 1736, page 228:
quote.text: Now, a famous King, and ſtrengthened with a Prince of ſingular expectation, and in the prime of his years, owner of the entire Iſle of Britain, enjoying Ireland populate and quiet, and infinitely more ſupported by Confederates of the Low-Countries, Denmarke, divers of the Princes of Germany and others.
